title: The Bangsamoro’s New Government Faces a Test of Public Trust
author: Haironesah Domado
text:
The parliament of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) in Cotabato City, Philippines.
Credit: Haironesah Domado
Last month’s parliamentary election in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) in the southern Philippines, the first ever, has settled one question but opened another.The election results are now clear. The Bangsamoro Federalist Party (BFP) secured 31 seats across the party and district races, the United Bangsamoro Justice Party (UBJP) 30, and the BARMM Grand Coalition (BGC) 15, with the remaining seats going to other parties and sectoral representatives. No party has the 41 votes needed to elect the chief minister. The 80 elected members of the first regular Parliament are set to assume office on October 30, marking the formal transition from the interim government to the first elected Bangsamoro government.[...]
